#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""HRV indices for a 5-minute resting ECG recording.

Pipeline (NeuroKit2 0.2.13 defaults):
  1. R-peak detection on the raw ECG column with the default "neurokit"
     finder at sampling_rate=100, correct_artifacts=False (no artifact
     correction, no pre-cleaning, no substituted detector).
  2. NN interval series (ms) from the detected peak indices at 100 Hz.
  3. nk.hrv_time, nk.hrv_frequency (normalize=True, Welch interpolation
     onto a 100 Hz grid), nk.hrv_nonlinear at default settings, and the
     combined nk.hrv table (column-wise concatenation of the three
     domains; no RSP-derived indices).

Undefined indices (e.g. HRV_ULF, SDANN2/SDNNI2/SDANN5/SDNNI5 for a
5-minute recording) are written as empty CSV fields via na_rep="".
"""
import argparse
import os

import pandas as pd
import neurokit2 as nk


def main():
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser()
    parser.add_argument("--input-dir", required=True)
    parser.add_argument("--output-dir", required=True)
    args = parser.parse_args()

    data = pd.read_csv(os.path.join(args.input_dir, "bio_resting_5min_100hz.csv"))
    ecg = data["ECG"]
    sampling_rate = 100

    # Step 1: R-peak detection, default "neurokit" finder, raw ECG,
    # no artifact correction.
    _, info = nk.ecg_peaks(
        ecg,
        sampling_rate=sampling_rate,
        method="neurokit",
        correct_artifacts=False,
    )
    peaks = info["ECG_R_Peaks"]

    os.makedirs(args.output_dir, exist_ok=True)

    # Steps 2-6: domain computations at the reference preset defaults.
    hrv_t = nk.hrv_time(peaks, sampling_rate=sampling_rate)
    hrv_f = nk.hrv_frequency(peaks, sampling_rate=sampling_rate, normalize=True)
    hrv_n = nk.hrv_nonlinear(peaks, sampling_rate=sampling_rate)
    # Combined table: domain functions at default settings (PSD
    # normalization on), concatenated column-wise; no RSP columns passed.
    hrv_all = nk.hrv(peaks, sampling_rate=sampling_rate)

    for frame, filename in (
        (hrv_t, "hrv_time.csv"),
        (hrv_f, "hrv_freq.csv"),
        (hrv_n, "hrv_nonlinear.csv"),
        (hrv_all, "hrv_indices.csv"),
    ):
        frame.to_csv(
            os.path.join(args.output_dir, filename),
            index=False,
            na_rep="",  # undefined indices -> empty fields
        )


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()
rationale: Implementation runs the reference preset directly: it reads only the ECG column, detects R-peaks with nk.ecg_peaks(method="neurokit", sampling_rate=100, correct_artifacts=False) on the raw series (no cleaning, no artifact correction), then computes nk.hrv_time, nk.hrv_frequency with normalize=True (Welch PSD on the 100 Hz interpolated NN grid), nk.hrv_nonlinear, and the combined nk.hrv table at default settings, writing each as a single-row CSV with header only and na_rep="" so undefined indices (HRV_ULF, HRV_SDANN2/SDNNI2/SDANN5/SDNNI5) are empty fields. Verified end-to-end on the supplied input: 431 R-peaks detected, all four files written with the full default index sets (25 time, 10 frequency, 60 non-linear, 95 combined; empty fields only for the undefined 5-minute indices), completing in about one second, within the 600 s limit. Output values are produced by the installed neurokit2==0.2.13, matching the requested definitions; the only recorded limitation is that agreement with the hidden reference values has been inferred from executing the same pinned library default call path, not independently recomputed (numerical equality is expected but was not separately verified in this session). CSV output precision is pandas default full repr of float64 (no lossy rounding introduced at this hand-off boundary).
